####################################################################################################
Purpose: To read data from GSK studies, specifically selecting relevant data frames (pid, 
demo, dates, expo, and sero_cod) and variables within those data frames. This script includes checks 
to ensure that the data has been tidied correctly.

Functions Used:
- `fun_dgsk_readdfs.R`: Reads the selected data frames, handling different formats (CDI or non-CDI).
- `fun_dgsk_exceptions.R`: Manages specific modifications required for individual study data.
- `fun_dgsk_tidynames.R`: Creates dictionaries for country, vaccine, and serology names.
- `fun_dgsk_tidydfs.R`: Selects variables within each data frame and sets appropriate data classes.
- `fun_dgsk_tidydates.R`: Converts GSK date formats into R-compatible formats.

Output (for each study):
- `stu_df_pid_{stu_id}.rds`: Processed participant data frame for the study.
- `stu_df_expoall_{stu_id}.rds`: Processed vaccine data frame for the study.
- `stu_df_seroall_{stu_id}.rds`: Processed serology data frame for the study.
####################################################################################################

# Load packages, themes, directories, and functions
```{r}
rm(list = ls())
source("00_pck.R")
source("fun_data/fun_dgsk_readdfs.R")
source("fun_data/fun_dgsk_exceptions.R")
source("fun_data/fun_dgsk_tidynames.R")
source("fun_data/fun_dgsk_tidydfs.R")
source("fun_data/fun_dgsk_tidydates.R")

# Function to check the percentage of missing values (NAs) per column, and to verify the number of 
# participants and duplicated rows
fun_checknas <- function(x) {
  # Arguments: 
  # - x: A data frame to be checked 
  x %>%
    # Add a column for the total number of rows
    mutate(length = n()) %>%
    group_by(study, length) %>%
    # Summarize the number of NAs per column
    summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.x))), .groups = "drop") %>%
    # Add columns for the number of distinct rows and the number of distinct PIDs (participants)
    mutate(length_distinct = length(distinct(x)[[1]]),
           length_pid = length(distinct(x, pid)[[1]])) 
  }
```

# Load the list of included studies and their contained directory
```{r}
# Load the data frame of studies 
stu_included <- readRDS(glue("{dirs$processed}/stu_included.rds"))
# Extract the study IDs and folders into a named vector
stu_l <- stu_included$stu_pat_tidy
names(stu_l) <- stu_included$study

# Filter to include only studies that have been marked as included
stu_l <- stu_l[!(names(stu_l) %in% filter(stu_included, included == FALSE)$study)]
```

# Read in and process data frames
```{r}
# Save the processed data frames?
saving <- FALSE
# Initialize a list to store various checks for each study
stu_che <- list("lengths" = list(), "contained" = list(), "naspid" = list(), "nasexpo" = list(), 
                "nassero" = list(), "numres" = list())

# Loop over each study to read, process, save, and check data frames
for(stu_id in names(stu_l)) {
  
  # Read in data frames ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
  # Determine if the study uses CDI format
  if(stu_id %in% c("115648", "115158", "115649", "115461", "201532")) cdi <- TRUE else cdi <- FALSE
  # Read the data frames for the current study 
  stu_dfs <- fun_dgsk_readdfs(study = stu_l[stu_id], cdi = cdi)
  
  # Pre-processing checks --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Record the length of each data frame (number of rows)
  stu_che$lengths[[stu_id]] <- lapply(stu_dfs, function(x) {length(x[[1]])})
  # Capture the names of studies contained within each data frame, if the "study" column exists
  stu_che$contained[[stu_id]] <- bind_rows(lapply(stu_dfs, function(dfs_i) {
    if(any(str_detect(names(dfs_i), "study"))) {
      distinct(dfs_i[str_subset(names(dfs_i), "stud")]) %>%
        rename_with(~ paste0("contained_", .x))
    }
  }), .id = "dfs")

  # Apply study-specific exceptions ----------------------------------------------------------------
  stu_dfs <- fun_dgsk_exceptions(stu_dfs, study_id = stu_id)
  
  # Create dictionaries for countries, vaccines, and serology names --------------------------------
  dics <- list()
  if(!cdi) { 
    # Non-CDI format
    dics$countries <- distinct(stu_dfs$pid, cty_nam) 
    dics$vaccines <- distinct(stu_dfs$expo, vaccine) 
    dics$seronames <- distinct(stu_dfs$sero, seroname, unit, method, cut_off)
  } else { 
    # CDI format
    dics$countries <- distinct(rename(stu_dfs$pid, cty_nam = country), cty_nam) 
    dics$vaccines <- distinct(rename(stu_dfs$expo, vaccine = aextrt), vaccine)
    dics$seronames <- distinct(filter(stu_dfs$sero, str_detect(param, "LOG10", negate = T)) %>%
                         mutate(unit = NA) %>%
                         rename(seroname = param, method = parcat1, cut_off = cutoff01), 
                       seroname, unit, method, cut_off)
  }
  # Standardize and tidy up names for countries, vaccines, and serology terms
  dics$countries <- fun_dgsk_tidynames(dics$countries, study = stu_id, tidynames = "country") 
  dics$vaccines <- fun_dgsk_tidynames(dics$vaccines, study = stu_id, tidynames = "vaccine") 
  dics$seronames <- fun_dgsk_tidynames(dics$seronames, study = stu_id, tidynames = "seroname") 
  
  # Append to or create the larger dictionary for each category and save 
  for(i in 1:length(dics)) {
    if(!file.exists(glue("{dirs$processed}/stu_tidynames_{names(dics)[i]}.rds"))) {
      # If the dictionary file doesn't exist, create it
      saveRDS(dics[[i]], glue("{dirs$processed}/stu_tidynames_{names(dics)[i]}.rds")) 
    } else { 
      # If it exists, append the new data and save
      dics[[i]] %>%
      bind_rows(filter(readRDS(glue("{dirs$processed}/stu_tidynames_{names(dics)[i]}.rds")), 
                         study != stu_id)) %>%
      saveRDS(glue("{dirs$processed}/stu_tidynames_{names(dics)[i]}.rds")) 
    }}
  
  # Tidy up pid, expo, and sero data frames --------------------------------------------------------
  # Pid data frame: study, pid, center, country, rct_group, eligibility, age, age_unit, sex, 
  # birth_date, birth_week, age_date
  df_pid <- fun_dgsk_tidydfs(stu_dfs, study_id = stu_id, cdi = cdi, dfs = "pid")
  # Expo data frame: study, pid, vaccine, group_nb, v_adm, vac_date
  df_expo <- fun_dgsk_tidydfs(stu_dfs, study_id = stu_id, cdi = cdi, dfs = "expo")
  # Sero data frame: study, pid, method, seroname, num_res, date_sero, activity
  df_sero <- fun_dgsk_tidydfs(stu_dfs, study_id = stu_id, cdi = cdi, dfs = "sero_all")

  # Post-processing checks -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Ensure that all age units are valid and among the expected values
  stopifnot(all(df_pid$age_unit %in% c("YEARS", "Y", "MONTHS", "M", "WEEKS", "W", "DAYS", "D", NA)))
  
  # Check for NAs and record the length, distinct length, and pid length for each data frame
  stu_che$naspid[[stu_id]] <- fun_checknas(df_pid)
  stu_che$nasexpo[[stu_id]] <- fun_checknas(df_expo)
  stu_che$nassero[[stu_id]] <- fun_checknas(df_sero)
  
  # Ensure that all introduced NAs in serology measurements are actual NAs and not limit values
  stu_che$numres[[stu_id]] <- unique(stu_dfs$sero$num_res[is.na(as.numeric(stu_dfs$sero$num_res))])
  
  # Save processed data frames ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  if(saving == TRUE) {
    saveRDS(df_pid, glue("{dirs$processed}/01_stu_tidydfs/stu_df_pid_{stu_id}.rds"))
    saveRDS(df_expo, glue("{dirs$processed}/01_stu_tidydfs/stu_df_expo_{stu_id}.rds"))
    saveRDS(df_sero, glue("{dirs$processed}/01_stu_tidydfs/stu_df_sero_{stu_id}.rds"))
    }  
}

# Combine all check results into a single data frame and save it 
stu_che <- lapply(stu_che, function(checks) bind_rows(lapply(checks, as.data.frame), .id = "study"))
stu_che_old <- readRDS(glue("{dirs$processed}/01_stu_tidydfs/stu_checks.rds"))
if(saving == TRUE) { saveRDS(stu_che, glue("{dirs$processed}/01_stu_tidydfs/stu_checks.rds")) }
```

# Exploring the data, checks =======================================================================

# 1. Check the dictionaries for consistency and completeness
```{r}
# Country tidy names: Review and arrange the distinct tidy country names
readRDS(glue("{dirs$processed}/stu_tidynames_countries.rds")) %>%
  distinct(country_tidy) %>%
  arrange(country_tidy)
# Vaccine tidy names: Review and arrange the distinct tidy vaccine names
readRDS(glue("{dirs$processed}/stu_tidynames_vaccines.rds")) %>%
  distinct(vaccine_tidy) %>%
  arrange(vaccine_tidy)
# Serology tidy names: Review and arrange the distinct tidy serology names, including method and cutoff
readRDS(glue("{dirs$processed}/stu_tidynames_seronames.rds")) %>%
  #distinct(method_tidy) %>%
  #distinct(seroname_tidy) %>%
  distinct(method_tidy, seroname_tidy, cut_off) %>%
  arrange(cut_off)
```

# 2. Check for repeated studies based on identical data frame lengths
This step helps to identify possible follow-up or booster studies where data is grouped and shared 
across studies.
Note: Different lengths do not guarantee that studies are not contained within others.
```{r}
# Identify studies with identical data frame lengths (indicating potential duplicates)
stu_che$lengths %>%
  arrange(pid) 

# Check if there are potential duplicates 
length(distinct(stu_che$lengths, pid, demo, dates, expo, sero)[,1]) == length(stu_che$lengths[,1])
```

# 3. Check for studies that contain other studies 
Some studies may include data from other studies, indicated by a column named "study."
```{r}
# Identify studies that might contain other studies (26 studies found)
# Note: Studies that contain other studies were excluded from the analysis.
stu_che$contained %>%
  pivot_longer(starts_with("contained"), values_to = "contained") %>%
  filter(!is.na(contained)) %>%
  distinct(study, contained) %>%
  mutate(across(-c("study"), ~str_replace(.x, "_", "-"))) %>%
  group_by(study) %>%
  # Check if each study contains itself (all studies do except for study 217744-097, which was wrongly named)
  mutate(base_check = any(contained == study)) %>%
  filter(study != contained) %>%
  # Determine if the contained studies are included in the list of studies to analyze (none)
  mutate(included = contained %in% names(stu_l)) %>%
  filter(included == TRUE)
```

# 4. Check for repetitions within the data frames in each study  
This check ensures that there are no unintended repetitions within the data frames, such as when
the dictionary might have named a vaccine or seroname the same across different entries, even though
it was considered different within the study (this should not happen).
```{r}
# Check for repetitions within the `pid`, `expo`, and `sero` data frames for each study
lapply(list(stu_che$naspid, stu_che$nasexpo, stu_che$nassero), function(x) {
  x %>%
  select(study, length, length_distinct, length_pid) %>%
  filter(length != length_distinct) 
})
```

# 5. Check the missing values (NAs)
This step evaluates the presence of NAs across the `pid`, `expo`, and `sero` data frames for each study.
```{r}
lapply(list(stu_che$naspid, stu_che$nasexpo, stu_che$nassero), function(x) {
  x %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  filter(sum(c_across(-c(study, starts_with("length"))), na.rm = TRUE) != 0) %>%
  mutate(across(-c(study, starts_with("length")), ~round(.x/length*100)))
})
```

# Extra: Checking a single study in detail ========================================================
# This section provides a way to drill down into the details of a specific study.
```{r}
# Select a specific study by its ID
study_pat <- "113808"

# Load the raw data for the selected study
stu_dfs <- fun_dgsk_readdfs(stu_l[study_pat], cdi = F, info_files = F)

# Load the tidied data frames for the selected study
df_pid <- readRDS(glue("{dirs$processed}/01_stu_tidydfs/stu_df_pid_{study_pat}.rds"))
df_expo <- readRDS(glue("{dirs$processed}/01_stu_tidydfs/stu_df_expo_{study_pat}.rds"))
df_sero <- readRDS(glue("{dirs$processed}/01_stu_tidydfs/stu_df_sero_{study_pat}.rds"))

# Load the dictionaries for the selected study
readRDS(glue("{dirs$processed}/stu_tidynames_countries.rds")) %>%
  filter(study %in% c(study_pat))
readRDS(glue("{dirs$processed}/stu_tidynames_vaccines.rds")) %>%
  filter(study %in% c(study_pat))
readRDS(glue("{dirs$processed}/stu_tidynames_seronames.rds")) %>%
  filter(study %in% c(study_pat))

# Load the vacc_con data for the selected study (if available)
if (any(str_detect(list.files(dirs$server_vacc_con, full.names = TRUE), study_pat))) {
readRDS(str_subset(list.files(dirs$server_vacc_con, full.names = TRUE), study_pat)) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.character)) %>%
  rename_with(tolower) %>%
  arrange(pid)
}
# Plot the presence of NAs across the data frames
(gg_miss_var(df_pid, facet = study) | gg_miss_var(df_expo) | gg_miss_var(df_sero)) / 
  (gg_miss_var(df_pid, show_pct = TRUE) | gg_miss_var(df_expo, show_pct = TRUE) | gg_miss_var(df_sero, show_pct = TRUE))
```
